output.best_reason: Version E has the most distinct voice: Félix is prickly, self-aware, and evasive, and his bitterness ("Clear. Yes. That is what frightens me") gives the strongest tension ending. The timestamps come out in argument and irritation rather than as a list. Its weak spot is a few meta-wink lines ("so that you do not have to write it twice") that break the illusion. Version B is close behind, with vivid period-tinged similes ("like a dead fish," "like a priest at the elevation") and an emotional close, but it repeats "When the temple struck nine" awkwardly and leans on the "I know how this looks" beat. Version A is clean and controlled with good jokes-under-fear characterization, but tension is more moderate. Version D has sharp interrogator pressure ("I am asking what you did"), though its repeated "Do you see how that looks?" tics wear thin. Version C is the most restrained and has nice period texture (the goose, Chopin when she is unhappy), but it has the least tension and reads as the most generic.
